working_memory.text: Growers at the Pellham orchard have confirmed an outbreak of Varley blight on roughly a third of their older pear trees. The fungus spreads in wet springs and shows first as dark rings on new leaves. The orchard has begun a copper spray programme and has pulled affected fruit from its farm shop as a precaution. Neighbouring farms have been asked to inspect their own trees weekly until midsummer. The orchard expects a smaller harvest but says the younger plantings on the south slope are so far unaffected.
